summary_for_children: Surah Hud tells how Nuh built the ark and was carried safely, and how Hud, Salih, Ibrahim, Lut and Shu'ayb called their peoples.
environment_concept: The ark coast, following 11:36-48: a shipyard where the ark's last planks are fitted (11:37), the loading ground where animals come aboard two by two and the weather turns (11:40), a stormy bay with waves like mountains (11:42), the green slopes where the ark rests (11:44), and an empty tent with a roasted calf for guests (11:69). Nuh, his family and the guests are never shown; the animal kinds are the artist's choice.
architecture_and_scenery: Timber shipyard, rising flood plain, high waves, a mountain slope, and a tent where guests are welcomed.

palette.lighting: Grey storm light to clear sun
palette.atmosphere: Rain, wind, rising water, then clean air

activities.name: Build the ark
activities.description: Carry four planks to the glowing gaps on the ark's frame; when all are fitted the hull is complete.
activities.label: artistic educational adaptation, not an event in the Quran

activities.name: Fair measure
activities.description: Balance a market scale so everyone receives full measure.
activities.label: artistic educational adaptation, not an event in the Quran

activities.name: Two of each kind
activities.description: Guide the animals aboard in pairs: each pair goes to its own pen (giraffes, camels, sheep, elephants), and the food and water go to the hold. Then the rain begins. The kinds of animals are the artist's choice; the Quran says "of each [creature] two mates".
activities.label: artistic educational adaptation, not an event in the Quran

narration_plan: The narrator follows the Quran's order of events and labels added detail as explanation.

story_library.source: Owner's 'Quran Adventure — Children's Story Library' (2026-11-04), first-draft narration for ages about 7-12
story_library.title: The Messengers and Their People
story_library.children_narration: Long ago, Allah sent messengers to guide different communities. Prophet Nuh warned his people and built an ark as Allah commanded. Prophet Hud called the people of 'Ad to worship Allah, while Prophet Salih brought a message to Thamud. Prophet Shu'ayb reminded his people to be honest in business. Each community had important choices to make. Some listened, while others refused. Their stories remind us that strength, wealth, or impressive buildings do not make anyone greater than Allah's guidance.
story_library.story_chapters: Nuh and the flood (11:25–49); Hud and 'Ad (11:50–60); Salih and the she-camel (11:61–68); Ibrahim's guests and Lut's people (11:69–83); Shu'ayb and honest trade (11:84–95); Musa and Pharaoh (11:96–99).

world_idea.title: The Valley of Civilizations
world_idea.description: Children explore six distinct historical landscapes. One chapter involves examining the wooden ark, another discovering the she-camel narrative, and another using real weighing scales to understand honest trade.

story_library.checks: Every reference exists in the verified text (checked 2026-11-04). Narration is draft, written by the owner, not reviewed by a scholar.
story_library.rule_conflicts_resolved: Six story chapters kept. The ark chapter is the existing Ark slice (11:37-44). Destroyed peoples (11:58-68, 11:82-83, 11:94-95) are reading places only; no punishment shown.
